question.text: The IC of Himalaya Arbitrage Fund (Cat III) is considering a merger-arb position. The deal is announced but board/regulatory approvals are PENDING. Which adjustment should the manager MOST appropriately make?

answer.text: Go fully long the target and short the acquirer at announcement price.
Wait until after shareholder approval to enter — the spread is gone by then.
Buy both target and acquirer aggressively, since all deals eventually close.
Size the position smaller than the theoretical arbitrage spread would justify, reflecting deal-break risk; consider buying deal-break protection.

explanation.text: The Logic: Pre-approval deals carry significant break risk. Prudent sizing + optional deal-break protection (e.g., OTM Puts on target, OTM Calls on acquirer as hedges) is the correct manager response per Section 10.1.4.2 risk discussion. The Trap: A ignores break risk. C is over-aggressive. D foregoes all alpha — spread compresses substantially post-approval. Cross-Exam Context: XIX-C covers same decision framework. XV (Research Analyst) covers break-probability modelling.
